newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Weather mostly good in Brazil soybean states - coops.
newsitem.headline: Weather mostly good in Brazil soybean states - coops.

text.p: Brazil's soybean crop was developing normally in the key growing region of Parana, but some areas of Rio Grande do Sul remained without rain and were starting to suffer losses, growers said.

"We've had rains in the region and skies remain covered," said Edson Luis de Soza, agronomist at the Copagril cooperative in Marechal Candido Rondon, Parana state. "It rained in practically the whole region on January 5, 8 and 9."
Parana was seeing typical summer weather with high temperatures and regular showers, he added.
In Prudentopolis, conditions were normal after nearly 50 mm of rain fell last week.

"Fifty percent of the crop is in the vegetative stage and 50 percent in the flowering stage," said Aniceto Bobato, agronomist at the Camp cooperative. Soil moisture was good and the temperature was 23 degrees Celsius early in the day.
But at the Cotrican cooperative in Candelaria, Rio Grande do Sul, growers were still waiting for rain and conditions were becoming critical.
"The same situation continues," said agronomist Marcos Ricardo Streck. The last significant rains were on December 19 and there were only isolated showers at the weekend.
"The early cycle soybean is already suffering losses of around 10 percent," Streck said. This was crop planted between November 1 and 15.
In some areas, the soybean has stopped developing during the vegetative growth stage due to drought.
